experiment: WG-6 WRITER GROUNDING — MODULAR ARBITRATION + SEMANTIC REPAIR CLOSURE

WG-6A.name: MODULAR VERDICT ARBITRATION
WG-6A.why_reuse_is_valid: WG-4A and WG-4B ran on the SAME frozen WG-3A extraction (236 parents, hashes verified identical). The arbitration layer under test is pure deterministic code, so the arbitrated verdict set is fully determined by artefacts that already exist.
WG-6A.that_flip_explained: GR2-02 (r2/P21). WG-4A had called it INTERPRETATION via the absence-as-evidence move; WG-4B's PROOF_TYPE NONE correctly overrides. A true positive, not a false positive.

WG-6A.wg5_false_positive: ELIMINATED BY CONSTRUCTION — exclusive routing, not a weakened negative-source rule. WG-4B's rule is byte-identical and still owns its class.

WG-6B.name: SEMANTIC REPAIR CLOSURE
WG-6B.new_licence_this_experiment: Repair may widen OLD_TEXT beyond the flagged span for semantic closure, but ONLY within the parent sentence of that finding. Enforced deterministically by the applier as a fail-closed containment assertion.

post_repair_reaudit.method: Full source-fidelity inspection of the PATCHED articles with the IDENTICAL instrument — frozen WG-3A extraction (sha 45586e5f...), then frozen WG-4A (sha 7a4937c9...) and frozen WG-4B (sha 3e4739d2...), then the SAME deterministic arbitration rule. No prompt was retyped or tuned.

This is DETECTOR RESAMPLING VARIANCE on untouched text, not repair-introduced invention.

closure_check.method: Per-patch semantic closure over the sentence AS IT NOW READS. The checker is deliberately NOT shown the pre-patch wording, so it judges the resulting commitment rather than whether strings disappeared.

FORM1-3-P3.basis: The calibrated post-repair detector flags NO unsupported content inside this repaired sentence. Gold V2.1's own min_correction for this finding is 'Remove the invented interval; keep only source-supported unfamiliarity' — exactly what the repair did. The same closure checker called the semantically equivalent R3-P1 sentence CLOSED, so it is internally inconsistent between the two.

R2-P2.basis: The checker's stated rationale — 'excised the main clause rather than the offending claim inside it' — is factually wrong. The patch removed exactly ' not because the review places them above the rest but simply'. The subject and the because-clause both survive: 'taken here because they can be set beside each other.' The patch removed no finite verb, so grammatical completeness is unchanged by the repair. Only collateral: the intensifier 'simply', which carries no factual commitment.

NEW_FINDINGS_NOT_PART_OF_THE_WG6_CHARTER.name: ARBITRATION_UNROUTED coverage gap — the pre-registered fallback fired for the first time
NEW_FINDINGS_NOT_PART_OF_THE_WG6_CHARTER.what: The router consults WG-4B's proof object only when WG-4A typed at least one commitment in the parent as SOURCE_META, or when the parent has exactly one commitment. In the post-repair run, form1-3/P83 was judged NEGATIVE with PROOF_TYPE NONE by WG-4B, but WG-4A decomposed that parent into two commitments (OTHER, HUMAN_STATE), neither typed SOURCE_META. The negative claim therefore had no routing target and WG-4B's UNSUPPORTED verdict was SUPPRESSED; WG-4A's INTERPRETATION stood.
NEW_FINDINGS_NOT_PART_OF_THE_WG6_CHARTER.consequence_here: Benign against frozen Gold V2.1, which does not list that proposition as unsupported — so the suppression happened to be correct.
NEW_FINDINGS_NOT_PART_OF_THE_WG6_CHARTER.consequence_in_general: A real recall hole. A genuinely unproven negative source claim sitting in a multi-commitment parent that WG-4A does not type SOURCE_META will silently escape the negative-source proof rule entirely.
NEW_FINDINGS_NOT_PART_OF_THE_WG6_CHARTER.why_it_did_not_show_in_WG-6A: WG-6A had 0 unrouted: both G13-04 and GR2-02 were typed SOURCE_META by WG-4A. The gap is latent in the pre-registered rule and only exposed by resampling.
NEW_FINDINGS_NOT_PART_OF_THE_WG6_CHARTER.recommended_fix: Make routing depend on WG-4B's own class judgement rather than requiring WG-4A to agree on the type — i.e. route on (IN_SCOPE=YES and NEGATIVE=YES) regardless of WG-4A commitment typing, applying the proof object to the parent. This must be measured, not assumed: it would have changed nothing in WG-6A but would flip form1-3/P83 to UNSUPPORTED post-repair.

NEW_FINDINGS_NOT_PART_OF_THE_WG6_CHARTER.name: Detector resampling variance on untouched prose
NEW_FINDINGS_NOT_PART_OF_THE_WG6_CHARTER.what: Re-running the identical frozen instrument over articles whose relevant sentences are byte-identical produced 2 UNSUPPORTED findings that the pre-repair run had judged INTERPRETATION, and changed extraction granularity (form1-3 81 -> 86 propositions, r3 74 -> 72).
NEW_FINDINGS_NOT_PART_OF_THE_WG6_CHARTER.consequence: The 'new unsupported: 0' gate cannot be read literally off a single resampled audit. Attribution must be done by checking whether the flagged text was touched by a patch — which is what was done here.
NEW_FINDINGS_NOT_PART_OF_THE_WG6_CHARTER.recommended_next: Quantify instrument variance directly (repeat the same audit on the same unmodified article N times) before treating any single post-repair count as an absolute gate.

SUCCESS_GATE_ASSESSMENT.WG-6B: 0 new unsupported: PASS ON ATTRIBUTION, NOT ON RAW COUNT — 0 introduced by patches; 2 appeared under the resampled instrument on prose no patch touched, both judged INTERPRETATION by the same instrument pre-repair. Recorded as WG6-N2, not as a repair defect.

decision_reasoning: Both defects WG-6 was chartered to fix are resolved. Defect 1 (false-positive composition): modular arbitration retains WG-4B's BOUNDED_ABSENCE distinction, the R3 control survives as SUPPORTED, and FP fell from 1 to 0 without touching the negative-source rule. Defect 2 (repair under-clearance): the residual visitor-state carrier is gone, all 8 gold unsupported are cleared, and the root cause of WG-5's failure is identified and fixed in the repair contract. Article Form and voice show no regression, so not D. Nothing under-clears, so not B. The one OVER_EDITED verdict is a checker artifact whose stated rationale is factually wrong about what was removed, so not C.
decision_caveat: Decision A rests on attributing the 2 post-repair unsupported findings to instrument resampling variance rather than to repair. That attribution is evidenced (byte-identical untouched text; the same instrument called both INTERPRETATION pre-repair) but it does mean the literal 'new unsupported = 0' reading of the gate was not met. Recorded openly as WG6-N2 so the owner can overrule.
architectural_result: MODULAR COMPOSITION IS SAFER THAN MONOLITHIC COMPOSITION. Keeping each calibrated component's judgement intact and composing only their VERDICTS through small deterministic arbitration preserved component behaviour that the WG-5 monolithic prompt destroyed, at equal recall and better precision. Repair closes commitments semantically when it is given the real parent sentence and a bounded licence to clear residual carriers within it. Two new issues are now on the table: a latent routing gap that suppresses a negative-source verdict when the components disagree about the claim's type, and measurable detector variance under resampling.
EXACT_NEXT_STEP: Close the WG6-N1 routing gap (route on WG-4B's own class judgement, re-score WG-6A to prove nothing regresses), then run ONE final untouched end-to-end shadow replay of the complete modular Writer Grounding pipeline. The replay was NOT run in this task.
